summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for dyspnea, cough, and worsening back pain. She had a history of HIV, which remained well-controlled, and was found to have a retrocardiac opacity on chest X-ray suggestive of atelectasis or mild pneumonia. She was treated with levofloxacin for presumed pneumonia and managed symptomatically for a viral upper respiratory infection. Her chronic back pain was stable on her home regimen, with no new neurological deficits. Urine culture showed low bacterial growth, and given her history of recurrent UTIs, no antibiotics were initiated. Her INR was subtherapeutic at 1.2, and warfarin was continued with plans for outpatient monitoring. She improved clinically, was discharged home on a five-day course of antibiotics, and with instructions to continue all home medications including pain management and anticoagulation.
problems: Acute upper respiratory infections of unspecified site
